verses.zh: 耶和华的话又临到我说：
verses.en: The Lord’s message came to me:

verses.zh: 「人子啊，你要发预言说，主耶和华如此说：哀哉这日！你们应当哭号。
verses.en: “Son of man, prophesy and say, ‘This is what the Sovereign Lord says:“‘Wail, “Alas, the day is here!”[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “Alas for the day.”
verses.commentary:
30:2 "prophesy" This VERB (BDB 612, KB 659) is a Niphal IMPERATIVE.
It is used thirty-seven times in Ezekiel. The book is a series of messages from YHWH to Judah through Ezekiel. How or when or
by whom they were gathered and combined is uncertain.

▣ "Thus says the Lord God" YHWH is the source of the message,
not Ezekiel (cf. Ezek. 25:3; Amos 1:3; 2:1).

▣ "Wail" This VERB (BDB 410, KB 413, Hiphil
IMPERATIVE) is common in

- Isaiah, 13:6; 14:31; 15:2,3; 16:7 (twice); 23:1,6,14; 52:5; 65:14

- Jeremiah, 4:8; 25:34; 47:2; 48:20,31,39; 49:3; 51:8

- Ezekiel (only twice), 21:12; 30:2

- Joel, 1:5,11,13

It denotes those who cry out like wounded animals at the judgment of God which has come upon them
(i.e. "Wail, also for the day!" Ezek. 30:2-3).

verses.zh: 因为耶和华的日子临近，就是密云之日，列国受罚之期。
verses.en: For the day is near,the day of the Lord is near;it will be a day of storm clouds,[NOTE:1] it will be a time of judgment[NOTE:2] for the nations.
notes: Heb “a day of clouds.” The expression occurs also in Joel 2:2 and Zeph 1:15; it recalls the appearance of God at Mount Sinai (Exod 19:9, 16, 18).
Heb “a time.” The words “of judgment” have been added in the translation for clarification (see the following verses).
verses.commentary:
30:3 "the day of the Lord" See note at Ezek. 7:19. This reference is to the
immediate invasion of Neo-Babylon, not an eschatological orientation.

Special Topic: The Day of the Lord

▣ "It will be a day of clouds" The phrase is an idiom of gloom (i.e. sirocco east winds from the
desert, cf. Ezek. 30:18; 32:7; 34:12), but it denotes more. The clouds are often the transportation of deity
(e.g. Jer. 4:13; Dan. 7:13; Nah. 1:3).

Special Topic: Coming On the Clouds

verses.zh: 必有刀剑临到埃及；在埃及被杀之人仆倒的时候，古实人就有痛苦，人民必被掳掠，基址必被拆毁。
verses.en: A sword will come against Egyptand panic will overtake Ethiopiawhen the slain fall in Egyptand they carry away her wealth and dismantle her foundations.
verses.commentary:
30:4 "anguish" This term (BDB 298) comes from "birth pains" (BDB 296). It describes the terrible pain,
emotionally and physically, of God's judgment

- against Philistia, Exod. 15:14

- against unspecified foreign kings, Ps. 48:6

- against Babylon, Isa. 13:8; 21:3; Jer. 50:43

- against Israel, Jer. 6:24; 22:23

- against Lebanon, Jer. 22:23

- against Moab, Jer. 48:41

- against Edom, Jer. 49:22

- against Egypt, Ezek. 30:4,9

- against Assyria, Nahum 2:10

Special Topic: Birth Pains

▣ "Ethiopia" This is literally "Cush" (BDB 468). Cush controlled Egypt during the twenty-fifth
dynasty (716-663 B.C.), but had since been overthrown. However, in Ezek. 30:4
and 9 "Cush" seems to be a designation for Egypt (cf. Isa. 20:4).

Special Topic: Kings of Egypt, I.

▣ "They take away her wealth" The term translated "wealth" (BDB 242) has several meanings.

- sound, murmur, roar of a crowd, Isa. 13:4; 17:12

- tumult, confusion, Isa. 33:3

- crowd, multitude, Ezek. 7:12,13; 23:42; 30:4; 39:11; Jer. 49:32

- abundance, Ps. 37:16; Eccl. 5:10; Isa. 60:5

Context must determine which fits best. Because of Ezek. 29:19 some choose #4, but 30:4 itself
supports #3. Notice the same ambiguity in Ezek. 30:10.

verses.zh: 古实人、弗人（或译：利比亚）、路德人、杂族的人民，并古巴人，以及同盟之地的人都要与埃及人一同倒在刀下。」
verses.en: Ethiopia, Put, Lud, all the foreigners,[NOTE:1] Libya, and the people[NOTE:2] of the covenant land[NOTE:3] will die by the sword along with them.
notes: The same expression appears in Exod 12:38; Jer 25:20; 50:37; Neh 13:3. It may refer to foreign mercenaries serving in the armies of the nations listed here.
Heb “sons.”
The expression “sons of the covenant land” possibly refers to Jews living in Egypt (Jer 44).
verses.commentary:
30:5 This verse refers to (1) mercenary soldiers (cf. Ezek. 30:8; 27:10) or (2) allies (i.e. "in league,"
Ezek. 30:5; and Ezek. 30:6,8).

- Ethiopia/Cush (BDB 468), cf. Ezek. 27:10; 38:5; Gen. 10:13

- Put/Libia (BDB 806), cf. Gen. 10:6; Jer. 46:9

- Lud/Lydia (BDB 530 [1] it is possible to link them with the northern Mediterranean, cf. Isa. 66:19
or [2] it is grammatically possible that all three denote Egypt)

- Arabia (Peshitta, BDB 787) or "mixed people" (LXX. NKJV, BDB 786), both have the same consonants

- Libya/Kub (see note below; BDB 464, cf. Gen. 10:13, another descendant of Ham living in
northeast Africa)

- "the people of the land," this phrase refers to another people group, but which one is uncertain.
Some commentators speculate that because the term "covenant"/berith is used it refers to Jews
living in north Africa (i.e. Jer. 44:1).

NASB, TEV, NRSV, NJB, Peshitta
"all Arabia"

NKJV
"all the mingled people"

REB
"all the Arabs"

JPSOA
"all the mixed populations"

LXX
"all these mixed in"

This verse is describing the people groups connected to Egypt that will experience the judgment
of YHWH. The Hebrew words

- mixed company ‒ ערב, BDB 786, cf. Jer. 25:20; 50:37

- Arabian ‒ ערבי, BB 787

are very similar. The UBS Text Project, p. 97, suggests option #1 with a "B" rating
(some doubt). It is PLURAL and may refer to mercenary troops.

NASB, NRSV, REB, LXX
"Libya"

NKJV, Peshitta
"Chub"

TEV
"Kub"

NJB, JPSOA
"Cub"

The MT has כיב (BDB 464; TEV, NJB, JPSOA, Peshitta) but many translations emend it
to לוב (BDB 530; LXX, NRSV, REB). The UBS Text Project, p. 98, gives the MT a "B" rating.

In the list of people groups allied with Egypt, Lud and Lydia are spelled similarly.

- Lud ‒ לוד (BDB 530)

- Lydia ‒ לוב (BDB 530)

verses.zh: 耶和华如此说：扶助埃及的也必倾倒。埃及因势力而有的骄傲必降低微；其中的人民，从色弗尼塔起（见二十九章十节）必倒在刀下。这是主耶和华说的。
verses.en: “‘This is what the Lord says:Egypt’s supporters will fall;her confident pride will crumble.[NOTE:1] From Migdol to Syene[NOTE:2] they will die by the sword within her, declares the Sovereign Lord.
notes: Heb “come down.”
Syene is known as Aswan today.
verses.commentary:
30:6 "the pride of her power will come down" This is the common thread between Tyre and Egypt (cf. Ezek. 28:2;
29:9b).

▣ "From Migdol to Syene" See note at Ezek. 29:10.

▣ "by the sword" YHWH sends the sword (cf. Ezek. 7:15). In this context, the sword is Nebuchadnezzar II's
army (cf. Ezek. 21; 30:10-11).

verses.zh: 埃及地在荒凉的国中必成为荒凉；埃及城在荒废的城中也变为荒废。
verses.en: They will be desolate among desolate lands,and their cities will be among ruined cities.

verses.zh: 我在埃及中使火着起；帮助埃及的，都被灭绝。那时，他们就知道我是耶和华。
verses.en: They will know that I am the Lordwhen I ignite a fire in Egyptand all her allies are defeated.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “all who aid her are broken.”

verses.zh: 「到那日，必有使者坐船，从我面前出去，使安逸无虑的古实人惊惧；必有痛苦临到他们，好像埃及遭灾的日子一样。看哪，这事临近了！
verses.en: “‘On that day messengers will go out from me in ships to frighten overconfident Ethiopia; panic will overtake them on the day of Egypt’s doom;[NOTE:1] for beware—it is coming!
notes: Heb “in the day of Egypt.” The word “doom” has been added in the translation to clarify the nature of this day.
verses.commentary:
30:9 Notice the words and phrases that refer to Egypt's day of judgment.

- "on that day"

- "on the day of Egypt"

- "it comes"

Special Topic: That Day

▣

NASB, NKJV, NRSV, TEV, NJB, REB
"in ships"

LXX, RSV, NEB
"rushing"

Peshitta
"in haste"

JPSOA
—

The MT has "in ship" (BDB 850). The UBS Text Project, p. 98, suggests this reading over the
LXX with a "B" rating (some doubt).

- in ship ‒ בצים (MT)

- hurrying ‒ אצים (LXX)

verses.zh: 主耶和华如此说：我必藉巴比伦王尼布甲尼撒的手，除灭埃及众人。
verses.en: “‘This is what the Sovereign Lord says:I will put an end to the hordes of Egypt,by the hand of King Nebuchadrezzar[NOTE:1] of Babylon.
notes: Heb “Nebuchadrezzar” is a variant and more exact spelling of Nebuchadnezzar, as the Babylonian name Nabu-kudurri-uṣur has an “r” rather than an “n.”
verses.commentary:
30:10 "hand" See Special Topic: Hand

▣ "Nebuchadnezzar" This is literally "Nebuchadressar." It is difficult to translate a foreign name into a new
language. This Neo-Babylonian king's name was "Nabu-Kudurri-usur," which may mean

- "Nebo, protect the boundary"

- "Nebo, watch over my heir (i.e. eldest son)"

- "Nebo, protect the crown"

- "Nebo, protect against misfortune"

The OT spells the name in three ways.

- נבוכדנצר

- נבוכדנאצר

- נבוכדרער

Special Topic: Nebo

verses.zh: 他和随从他的人，就是列国中强暴的，必进来毁灭这地。他们必拔刀攻击埃及，使遍地有被杀的人。
verses.en: He and his people with him, the most terrifying of the nations,[NOTE:1] will be brought there to destroy the land.They will draw their swords against Egyptand fill the land with corpses.
notes: The Babylonians were known for their cruelty (2 Kgs 25:7).
verses.commentary:
30:11 "The most ruthless of the nations" This phrase describes the mercenary army of Nebuchadnezzar II,
King of Neo-Babylon (cf. Ezek. 28:7; 31:12; 32:12; Hab. 1:6-8).

verses.zh: 我必使江河干涸，将地卖在恶人的手中；我必藉外邦人的手，使这地和其中所有的变为凄凉。这是我―耶和华说的。
verses.en: I will dry up the waterwaysand hand the land over to[NOTE:1] evil men.I will make the land and everything in it desolate by the hand of foreigners.I, the Lord, have spoken!
notes: Heb “and I will sell the land into the hand of.”
verses.commentary:
30:12 Notice the number of FIRST PERSON SINGULAR VERBS referring to YHWH's
sovereignty.

- I will make, BDB 678, KB 733,Qal PERFECT with waw

- I will sell, BDB 569, KB 581, Qal PERFECT with waw

- I will make (lit. "I will bring desolation"), BDB 1030, KB 1563, Hiphil
PERFECT with waw

- I, the Lord, have spoken, BDB 180, KB 210, Piel PERFECT

Number 2 is especially interesting because it uses a term normally reserved for YHWH's actions
toward unfaithful Israel (cf. Deut. 32:30; Jdg. 2:14; 3:8; 4:2,9; 10:7; 1 Sam. 12:9). The usage here implies
YHWH's ownership of all lands and all peoples (cf. Deut. 32:8).

"Sell" is imagery for giving a people group into the hand of another group. A nation loses its autonomy.

verses.zh: 主耶和华如此说：我必毁灭偶像，从挪弗除灭神像；必不再有君王出自埃及地。我要使埃及地的人惧怕。
verses.en: “‘This is what the Sovereign Lord says:I will destroy the idols,and put an end to the gods of Memphis.There will no longer be a prince from the land of Egypt;so I will make the land of Egypt fearful.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “I will put fear in the land of Egypt.”
verses.commentary:
30:13-19 Notice the list of Egyptian allies.

- Memphis, Ezek. 30:13,16, first known capital of Egypt named Menes after the first powerful king. Its
chief deity was Ptah, the creator-god. The later name, Memphis, came from its association
with the pyramid of Pepi I.

- Pathros, Ezek. 30:14, see note at Ezek. 29:14

- Zoan, Ezek. 30:14, also called Tanis and probably the Hyksos Avaris, later called Ramesses, the delta
capital of Egypt in 21st and 22nd dynasties (i.e. the area where Jacob settled)

- Thebes, Ezek. 30:14,16, is the location of the valleys of the kings and temples of Amun. Today it is
called Luxor, about 400 miles south of Cairo.

- Sin (LXX, Syene), Ezek. 30:15,16, a city is located in the delta. In Greek it is called Pelusium
(i.e. city of mud). It guarded the highway to the north.

- On (LXX, Heliopolis), Ezek. 30:17, this city is close to Cairo in the delta region. In Greek it is called
Heliopolis (i.e. city of the sun). It was one of the cities built by Hebrew slaves (cf. Exod. 1:11).

- Pi-beseth, Ezek. 30:17, later the capital of Egypt (22nd dynasty). It was named after
the goddess Bastet (woman with cat head). It was made famous by Pharaoh Shishak.

- Tehaphnehes, Ezek. 30:18, in Jer. 43:7 it is spelled Tahpanhes. It is located on the highway going to
Arabia in the eastern delta region.

30:13 "the idols" There were several categories of idols (BDB 156) in Egypt.

- royal rulers (Pharaohs)

- animals

- half human, half animals

- fertility gods

Each city had their own chief god and/or goddess.

▣ "images" This (BDB 47) is parallel to "idols." Its basic meaning is uncertain, but the same root in
Syriac means "weak," "feeble," "poor." It has the connotation of that which is insufficient or worthless.
It is translated "idols" in Leviticus 19:4; 26:1; Psalm 96:5; 97:7; Isa. 2:8,18,20(twice); 10:10; 19:1,3;
31:7(twice); Hab. 2:18.

▣ "there will no longer be a prince in the land of Egypt" Apparently Neo-Babylon's conquest and exile
completely removed all the royal family to Babylon. Pharoah Hophra was assassinated and a new dynasty started.

verses.zh: 我必使巴忒罗荒凉，在琐安中使火着起，向挪施行审判。
verses.en: I will desolate Pathros,I will ignite a fire in Zoan,and I will execute judgments on Thebes.
verses.commentary:
30:14 "Zoan" This is a Hebrew form of the name of a famous ancient city (cf. Num. 13:22) in the eastern
delta region that is known by several names.

- Avaris (Hyksos name)

- Pi-Ramesse (moved to a new location to the north which became Zoan, ABD, vol. 6, p. 1106)

- Tanis (later Greek name)

It was the northern capital of several Egyptian dynasties (i.e. Hyksos and Ramses II). It became the
site of a revival temple to Amon (original temple was at Thebes).

It is mentioned in the OT in Num. 13:22; Isa. 19:11,13; 30:4; Ezek. 30:14, as well as Ps. 78:12,43.

verses.zh: 我必将我的忿怒倒在埃及的保障上，就是训上，并要剪除挪的众人。
verses.en: I will pour out my anger upon Pelusium,[NOTE:1] the stronghold of Egypt;I will cut off[NOTE:2] the hordes of Thebes.
notes: Heb “Sin” (so KJV, NASB), a city commonly identified with Pelusium, a fortress on Egypt’s northeastern frontier.
Or “kill.”
verses.commentary:
30:15

NASB, NRSV, TEV
"Thebes"

NKJV, NJB, JPSOA, Peshitta
"No"

REB
"Noph"

LXX
"Memphis"

The MT has "No" (נא, BDB 609), which was later called Thebes. The NEB, REB have "Noph"
(נף, BDB 592), which was also called "Memphis" (LXX).

The UBS Text Project, p. 98, gives "No" a "B" rating (some doubt). Both "No" and "Memphis"
are mentioned in v. 16.

verses.zh: 我必在埃及中使火着起；训必大大痛苦；挪必被攻破；挪弗白日（或译：终日）见仇敌。
verses.en: I will ignite a fire in Egypt; Syene[NOTE:1] will writhe in agony, Thebes will be broken down,and Memphis will face enemies every day.
notes: The LXX reads “Syene,” which is Aswan in the south. The MT reads Sin, which has already been mentioned in v. 15.
verses.commentary:
30:16 "writhe in anguish" This VERB (BDB 296, KB 297) is repeated to
denote intensity (i.e. INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT and
IMPERFECT VERB).

▣ "will be breached" This is a Niphal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT
(BDB 131, KB 149). The TEV and NJB follow the Septuagint, which sees the breach as referring to the city's
(i.e. Thebes) walls breaking and letting the Nile flood the city. The Septuagint (LXX) does not mention
Memphis in the closing line of Ezek. 30:16.

verses.zh: 亚文和比伯实的少年人必倒在刀下；这些城的人必被掳掠。
verses.en: The young men of On and of Pi Beseth[NOTE:1] will die by the sword;and the cities will go[NOTE:2] into captivity.
notes: On and Pi Beseth are generally identified with the Egyptian cities of Heliopolis and Bubastis.

Heb “they will go.” The pronoun and verb are feminine plural, indicating that the cities just mentioned are the antecedent of the pronoun and the subject of the verb. The translation makes this clear by stating the subject as “the cities.”
verses.commentary:
30:17-18 The NASB translates "they" (a FEMININE PLURAL ) of Ezek. 30:17b as
"the women," while NKJV translates "they" as "these cities" (also FEMININE
in Hebrew), as do NRSV and NJB. The TEV identified "they" as other people.

The NASB probably bases its understanding on the parallelism of Ezek. 30:18e.

verses.zh: 我在答比匿折断埃及的诸轭，使她因势力而有的骄傲在其中止息。那时，日光必退去；至于这城，必有密云遮蔽，其中的女子必被掳掠。
verses.en: In Tahpanhes the day will be dark[NOTE:1] when I break the yoke of Egypt there. Her confident pride will cease within her;a cloud will cover her, and her daughters will go into captivity.
notes: In Zeph 1:15 darkness is associated with the day of the Lord.
verses.commentary:
30:18 "the day will be dark" Most English translations change the MT's "shall be withheld"
(BDB 362, חשׂך, JPSOA) to "will be darkened" (BDB 364, חשׁך, LXX, Peshitta).

▣ "the pride of her power will cease" Pride is a major spiritual problem for humans, angels, and
nations. It is the essence of the self-centeredness of Genesis 3. It is always followed by divine judgment
(e.g. Ezek. 28:2; 29:3; 32:12; 33:28; Isa. 14:13-14; 16:6; 25:11).

Special Topic: Lifted Up

verses.zh: 我必这样向埃及施行审判，他们就知道我是耶和华。」
verses.en: I will execute judgments on Egypt.Then they will know that I am the Lord.’”

verses.zh: 十一年正月初七日，耶和华的话临到我说：
verses.en: In the eleventh year, in the first month, on the seventh day of the month,[NOTE:1] the Lord’s message came to me:
notes: April 29, 587 b.c.
verses.commentary:
30:20-26 This is a new revelation about YHWH's judgment on Egypt, which uses the idiom of "arm" in several ways. Arm is imagery for ability.

- I have broken the arm of Pharaoh, Ezek. 30:21,22. Pharaoh Hophra gave himself the title of
"The Strong-Armed One." This is, therefore, powerful irony.

- It has not been bound up for healing, Ezek. 30:21

- Or wrapped with a bandage that it may be strong to hold the sword, Ezek. 30:21

- I will make the sword fall from his hands, Ezek. 30:22

- I will strengthen the arms of the king of Babylon, Ezek. 30:24,25

- I will put My sword in his hand, Ezek. 30:24,25

- I will break the arms of Pharaoh, Jer. 48:25

- The arms of Pharaoh will fall, Jer. 37:5

Special Topic: Hand

verses.zh: 「人子啊，我已打折埃及王法老的膀臂；没有敷药，也没有用布缠好，使他有力持刀。
verses.en: “Son of man, I have broken the arm[NOTE:1] of Pharaoh king of Egypt.[NOTE:2] Look, it has not been bandaged for healing or set with a dressing so that it might become strong enough to grasp a sword.
notes: The expression “breaking the arm” indicates the removal of power (Pss 10:15; 37:17; Job 38:15; Jer 48:25).
This may refer to the event recorded in Jer 37:5.

verses.zh: 所以主耶和华如此说：看哪，我与埃及王法老为敌，必将他有力的膀臂和已打折的膀臂全行打断，使刀从他手中坠落。
verses.en: Therefore this is what the Sovereign Lord says: Look,[NOTE:1] I am against[NOTE:2] Pharaoh king of Egypt, and I will break his arms, the strong arm and the broken one, and I will make the sword drop from his hand.
notes: The word הִנֵּה (hinneh) indicates becoming aware of something and has been translated here as a verb.

Or “I challenge.” The phrase “I am against you” may be a formula for challenging someone to combat or a duel. See D. I. Block, Ezekiel (NICOT), 1:201-2, and P. Humbert, “Die Herausforderungsformel ‘hinnenî ’êlékâ’” ZAW 45 (1933): 101-8.

verses.zh: 我必将埃及人分散在列国，四散在列邦。
verses.en: I will scatter the Egyptians among the nations and disperse them among foreign countries.

verses.zh: 我必使巴比伦王的膀臂有力，将我的刀交在他手中；却要打断法老的膀臂，他就在巴比伦王面前唉哼，如同受死伤的人一样。
verses.en: I will strengthen the arms of the king of Babylon, and I will place my sword in his hand, but I will break the arms of Pharaoh, and he will groan like the fatally wounded before the king of Babylon.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “him”; the referent has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 我必扶持巴比伦王的膀臂，法老的膀臂却要下垂；我将我的刀交在巴比伦王手中，他必举刀攻击埃及地，他们就知道我是耶和华。
verses.en: I will strengthen the arms of the king of Babylon, but the arms of Pharaoh will fall limp. Then they will know that I am the Lord when I place my sword in the hand of the king of Babylon and he extends it against the land of Egypt.

verses.zh: 我必将埃及人分散在列国，四散在列邦；他们就知道我是耶和华。」
verses.en: I will scatter the Egyptians among the nations and disperse them among foreign countries. Then they will know that I am the Lord.”

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible.
Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the four modern translations above.
Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: EZEKIEL 30:1-5

1The word of the Lord came again to me saying, 2"Son of man,
prophesy and say, 'Thus says the Lord God,

"Wail, 'Alas for the day!'

3For the day is near,

Even the day of the Lord is near;

It will be a day of clouds,

A time of doom for the nations.

4A sword will come upon Egypt,

And anguish will be in Ethiopia;

When the slain fall in Egypt,

They take away her wealth,

And her foundations are torn down.

5Ethiopia, Put, Lud all Arabia, Libya and the people of the land that is in league will fall with them by the sword."
